title: Behavior change: more argument names are refused in a macro sink
body: The credential sink guard shares the widened vocabulary, so names it did not know at 0.23.0 -- passphrase, pw, pwd, authorization, access_key, private_key, and plural forms -- are now refused when a macro expands them into a url, expression, verify_js or grabbed_predicate_js. OCTOWRIGHT_MACRO_CREDENTIAL_SINKS still defaults to block, so a macro that put {{access_key}} in a query string worked at 0.23.0 and raises at 0.23.1 with no config change on the operator's side. The opt-out is named in the error text and exists for exactly that case: OCTOWRIGHT_MACRO_CREDENTIAL_SINKS=allow. Measured across a 340-macro corpus on one machine, no macro was affected -- but a newly refused macro is what a different corpus would surface first, so read this as a behavior change with an opt-out, not only as a fix.

title: The sink guard missed five credential spellings
body: The guard defaults to block, so an operator is entitled to believe a credential-named argument cannot expand into a navigation or code sink. For those names it silently could. It matched on its own private name table, in which auth required an underscore or end-of-string boundary -- so authorization missed -- and only api_key and apikey were listed -- so access_key and private_key missed. {{password}} in a url was refused while {{passphrase}} expanded. No macro in the measured corpus used the affected names, which makes this a latent hole rather than live exposure; it becomes exposure the day someone names a parameter passphrase.

title: One credential vocabulary instead of three that disagreed
body: macros.privacy, artifacts.redaction and the macro sink guard each carried a private notion of which argument names are sensitive, and they disagreed 1173 times across a 1916-name corpus. private_key, cookie, cookies and set_cookie were caught by the redactor but missed by the macro classifier; otp was known only to the sink guard; plural forms bypassed all three. They now share one vocabulary -- the union of what all three matched at 0.23.0, with a match mode declared per token -- and a frozen baseline fixture asserts that no name any 0.23.0 classifier called sensitive became insensitive. artifacts.redaction is kept and held to the union by test, because lint_urls imports from it. Nothing outside macros/ and artifacts/script_export.py is touched: browser driving, personas, scenarios, goldens, the dashboard and the recorder's own input redaction are unaffected.

title: Regenerate exported scripts: a stale export carries the old table
body: ARG_PRIVACY_CLASSIFIER_VERSION moves from 2 to 3, and the matcher baked into an exported script is a copy, not a reference. A script exported before this release keeps classifying by the old table, so at runtime it will miss private_key, cookie, set_cookie, otp and every plural form the current classifier catches. Regenerating exports is remediation, not housekeeping. There is no staleness detection for this today; it is recorded as deferred work in the design spec rather than implemented here.
